definitions.explanation: Shoes made of leather, typically formal or business-style footwear. A standard part of business attire in Japan.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{革靴|かわぐつ}を{買|か}った。
{革靴|かわぐつ}が{雨|あめ}で{濡|ぬ}れてしまった。
examples.english: My leather shoes got wet in the rain.

examples.japanese: {面接|めんせつ}の{前日|ぜんじつ}に{革靴|かわぐつ}を{磨|みが}いて、{準備|じゅんび}を{整|ととの}えた。
examples.english: The day before the interview, I polished my leather shoes and got everything ready.

notes:
USAGE:
{革靴|かわぐつ} is standard vocabulary for business and formal contexts in Japan. New employees typically purchase {革靴|かわぐつ} as part of their business attire.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {革靴|かわぐつ}を{磨|みが}く (to polish leather shoes)
- {革靴|かわぐつ}を{履|は}く (to wear leather shoes)
- {革靴|かわぐつ}の{手入|てい}れ (leather shoe care)

RELATED WORDS:
- スニーカー: sneakers
- {靴|くつ}: shoes (general)
- {靴磨|くつみが}き: shoe polishing
- {長靴|ながぐつ}: boots, rain boots
